summary: Smyth County, VA tower site on Dickey Knob: built 1934 (date disputed), removed before 1994; only the foundation remains, reached on foot in Raccoon Branch Wilderness.

facts.design: 50 feet tall, with an enclosed 12×12 room at the top (no unit given in source)
facts.status_note: Register says removed before 1994; local history says it was torn down and that the foundation remains

access.note: Reached on foot by the Dickey Knob Trail from Raccoon Branch Campground in the Raccoon Branch Wilderness; the sources read describe hikes and mention no closures

visit.trail_note: No tower remains to climb. The Virginia Wilderness Committee says the trailhead is by site 6 in the campground; a hiker's account describes a 4.8-mile out-and-back that includes the summit

events.note: Register's build year. Local history says the exact date is unknown and that 1934 has been said, linked to a 1934 penny set in the USGS marker's cement

corrections.why: The Register's Removed field reads 'before 1994', so 1994 is a limit, not the year of removal. The 1994 event is dropped and the story says before 1994.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register gives 1934. The local history says the exact date is unknown and that 1934 has been said, based on a penny in the USGS marker's cement. The record keeps 1934 with that caveat in the note.

Register gives 3,697 ft (1,127 m); the local history cites the USGS marker at about 3,640 ft; a hiking blog gives 3,649 ft. Not resolved; the story gives the Register figure next to the local history figure.

The Virginia Wilderness Committee says the trail offers spectacular views today; the hiking blog found the summit enclosed in dense woods, with views at an overlook partway along the trail. The story reports both.

sources.title: History of the Dickeys Knob Fire Tower

notes_for_editor: Built year rests on the Register's 1934, which the local history calls unconfirmed; the removal is only 'before 1994', so the brief's 1994 event was dropped. Elevation differs across three sources (Register 3,697 ft, local history about 3,640 ft, hiking blog 3,649 ft); the Wikipedia Raccoon Branch article lists a different summit figure (3,606 ft for 'Dicky Knob') and was not used. Summit view is disputed between sources and the story reports both. Staffing date is from a photo caption only. The Register's footer photo (concrete footers) is credited to Jordan Dennison, but no image URL appeared in the text read, so no photo was added. Trail length in the Wikipedia listing (2.3 miles, one way) differs from the Wilderness Committee's 2.6 miles one way; the story avoids a trail length.
